key_insight: The transport Neural Tangent Kernel (tNTK) enables active learning that captures changes in both the mean and shape of predicted distributions, unlike mean-based approaches.
engineering_relevance: For expensive experiments with distributional outputs, tNTK can guide which conditions to measure next to improve conditional generative models.
method: Decompose Wasserstein test risk into mean and shape terms.
Use tNTK to measure predicted-distribution sensitivity to model parameters, with closed-form affine Gaussian calculations or Monte Carlo estimation.
Treat tNTK as a Gaussian process covariance and greedily select inputs that minimize total posterior variance across the candidate pool.
evidence_signal: Across four conditional generative model classes evaluated on synthetic distributions, intent-labeled sentences, and single-cell perturbation responses, tNTK outperformed the conditional-mean NTK baseline.
watch_item: Outside affine Gaussian settings, Monte Carlo estimation adds computational cost, and the posterior Fréchet variance bound assumes small parameter perturbations.
paper_title: Active Learning of Conditional Generative Models via the Transport Neural Tangent Kernel
